messages:
Anjali: Heads-up: saw a perf + quality regression on the mixed FP8/INT8 path in canary. p99 went up ~120ms, tokens/sec down ~18%. Eval runs show a ~7% increase in hallucination on our structured JSON outputs. Repro: run the canary model with default kernel selector and run eval-suite/structured-json.
Tom: @Anjali can you link the perf dashboard and paste the eval diff? also which commit touched kernel selection?
Anjali: dashboard: https://redwood.example.com/perf/abcd - eval diffs attached (summary): structured-hallucination +7%, exact-match down 2.3%. Kernel selector change: commit 8f3a2b9 (prefer fused_fp8kernel for seq<=128 then fallback). Repro command: ```bash
# reproduce eval
REDWOOD_ENV=canary \
REDWOOD_MODEL=canary-mix-1 \
./tools/run_eval --suite structured-json --warmup 200 --iters 1000
```
Priya: I ran a quick perf profile on the canary instance. Flamegraph points to a big hotspot in quant::dequantize for the int8 fallback path; the fused_fp8kernel does less copy but when it falls back we dequantize+memcpy a lot. Snippet from perf top: ```
25.3% quant::dequantize
12.1% kv_cache::write_prefix
9.8% memcpy
8.2% attention::matmul
```
Luis: FYI I instrumented KV cache hit rates. Before the selector change we had ~98% prefix hits for typical traffic. After the fused_fp8 preference it's ~84% — seems kernels expect different padding/seq rounding which changes how we compute cache keys, causing more prefix recompute and higher latency.
Tom: quick mitigation: force the previous selector until triage done: ```bash
export REDWOOD_KERNEL_SELECTOR=stable
systemctl restart redwood-runtime
```
perf-bot: auto-summary: p50 ~+10ms, p95 ~+60ms, p99 ~+120ms, tokens/sec -18%. Memory churn and increased memcpy events detected. Correlates with selector commit 8f3a2b9.
Anjali: Plan: run small matrix and report: (1) revert selector commit, (2) force kernel env, (3) run per-layer int8 calibration (pcalib v2), (4) cap batch-size to 8 to limit memcpy amplification. Who takes which runs?
Priya: I can run calibration + eval diffs. I'll use this calib config: ```json
{"calib_mode":"per-layer-statistics","per_channel":true,"num_calib_samples":1024}
``` I will post results here.
Luis: I'll test a kv-pad normalization patch to make cache keys consistent across kernels; if that fixes hit-rate we shouldn't need to revert selector.
Tom: I'll open a rollback PR in case we need a hot revert and coordinate canary cutover. If calib fixes hallucinations without perf loss we prefer that.
Anjali: Great. Please drop quick numbers here as you get them. tagging @Tom @Priya @Luis. :thumbsup:
